# SAIPEN audit-manifest contract fixtures

Canonical, unedited output of the REAL SAIPEN generator, kept here so the
contract regression suite can prove AUDAPACK reads what the protocol actually
writes — not a shape AUDAPACK imagined the protocol writes.

| File | Contract | Provenance |
|------|----------|------------|
| `MANIFEST.v1.json` | `contract_version: 1` | Copied byte-for-byte from a live project enrolled by the v1-era generator (`_SAIPENVIEW/.saipen/MANIFEST.json`, sha256 `c688c752afc20ff1…`). It is the *only* honest source for v1: the canonical install at `V:\…\_SAIPEN` now writes v2, so a freshly generated v1 document no longer exists. |
| `MANIFEST.v2.json` | `contract_version: 2` | Generated by the current canonical generator (`V:\…\_SAIPEN\tools\saipen.py audit manifest --write`, `CONTRACT_VERSION = 2`) inside a controlled fixture checkpoint, then copied unmodified (sha256 `f9536658302349cf…`). |
| `MANIFEST.v3.json` | `contract_version: 3` | Captured byte-for-byte from the live AUDAPACK project's own `.saipen/MANIFEST.json` (generator `saipen-audit-manifest/3`). v3 is a forward-compatible superset of v2: same core evidence shape plus additive metadata (`nested_instance_files`, `non_exportable_filenames`, `non_exportable_segments`, `non_exportable_suffixes`, `precedence`). AUDAPACK reads it in COMPATIBLE_DEGRADED mode — no new parser required. |

## What v2 actually changed

Taken from these two real documents, not inferred from prose. Everything the
consumer reads is IDENTICAL in both shapes except:

* `contract_version`: `1` → `2`
* `generator`: `saipen-audit-manifest/1` → `saipen-audit-manifest/2`
* `evidence.non_exportable`: v2 adds `quarantine/`

`required`, `compatibility`, `references`, the mandatory-file objects and every
bounded conditional/optional directory rule are byte-identical between the two
versions. That is why `parse_contract_v1` and `parse_contract_v2` share their
body and differ only where the contract differs — and why v2 is additionally
held to `quarantine/` even if a drifted document drops it.

## Regenerating the v2 fixture

```bash
python <saipen_home>/tools/saipen.py \
    --project-root <fixture-with-.saipen-checkpoint> \
    audit manifest --write
```

`--project-root` must be passed explicitly: the CLI resolves the project root
independently of the working directory, so a fixture without it silently
resolves to the nearest enclosing enrolled project.

Two SAIPEN installs can disagree on `CONTRACT_VERSION` — a stale skill copy
next to the canonical checkout. The fixtures above come from the canonical
install named by `.saipen/STATE.md`'s `saipen_home`.

## Cross-repo tripwire

`tests/test_saipen_contract_compat.py` verifies both committed fixtures and,
when a SAIPEN authority is present on this machine, generates a fresh manifest
with the real CLI and requires AUDAPACK to support the version it declares. That
is the check that was missing when SAIPEN moved to v2 and AUDAPACK kept
answering `PROTOCOL_CONTRACT_UNKNOWN` at pack time.
